AttributesList.AttributeDescription: The sources describe what the project does and why it should work, but give no data on results. Protocol code L1.
The sources give data on activity, such as payments made or users reached, but not on whether people are better off. Protocol code L2.
The sources report changes for participants, such as income or savings, with nothing to compare against. Protocol code L3.
The sources compare participants with a similar group or a non-blockchain alternative. Protocol code L4.
A randomised trial or strong quasi-experimental study estimates the project's impact. Protocol code L5.
Transaction cost, speed, administrative burden.
Adoption, active use, inclusion of women, unbanked people and displaced people.
Traceability, leakage, fraud, user trust.
Income, savings, coping, financial stress.
Health, education, climate adaptation, human rights and justice, culture.
Privacy, volatility, cash-out failure, exclusion, security incidents.
Humanitarian cash, anticipatory cash, remittances, merchant payments, wages.
Micro-lending, savings tools, parametric insurance, guarantees.
Digital ID, credentials, provenance, archiving and storage.
Vaccines, food, commodities, tokenised goods.
Carbon and environmental credits, regenerative finance, climate data.
DAOs, community treasuries, crowdfunding, grant and donor flows.
No domain fits; explained in a note. Connectivity and information access are coded here (rule D5). Counts toward taxonomy fit (metric 3).
A time-bound test with named users (GSR-confirmed, Gate 1).
Continued or enlarged by the same operator, still described as a pilot.
Same solution used beyond the pilot period with wider reach as routine operation (a deployment).
Used by a new operator such as a government, partner or country office (a deployment).
Sources say the use case ended or the organisation closed.
Sources do not state what happened after the pilot.
Sources say blockchain helped, with no comparison.
Descriptive comparison with a prior or alternative channel.
Tested comparison against a non-blockchain alternative on the same outcome; only when the comparison isolates the ledger (rule V1).
